name: App development
heading:
A good idea.
A great experience.
copy: Native and cross-platform apps with considered interfaces, reliable performance, and engineering that lasts.
icon: <rect x="7" y="3" width="22" height="30" rx="4"/><path d="M14 7h8M14 28h8"/><path class="accent" d="M12 20l4-4 3 3 5-6"/>
title: Mobile App Development
description: Mobile app development for iOS and Android. Project 0 designs and builds native and cross-platform apps, with the backend systems behind them.
intro: An app should make a useful idea easy to use. We connect product thinking, interface design, and mobile engineering so the experience holds together from the first screen to the systems behind it.
audience: For teams launching a new mobile product, improving an existing app, or bringing a service to iOS and Android.
offers: iOS and Android apps
Native and cross-platform development, with the approach chosen around the experience, device features, and maintenance needs of your product.
Product flows and interface design
Turn a rough idea into clear journeys, prototypes, and interfaces. Work through onboarding, core tasks, empty states, and the details people meet every day.
Connected product engineering
Build the APIs, authentication, and integrations an app depends on. Consider loading, failures, and unreliable connections as part of the experience.
steps: Define the first useful release
Map the users, key tasks, platform requirements, and existing systems. Agree on a focused scope before implementation.
Design and build together
Prototype important journeys and ship working increments. Review real screens and behaviours as the product takes shape.
Prepare for real-world use
Test on target devices, review performance and accessibility, and work through release and ongoing maintenance requirements.
faqs: Native or cross-platform: which should we choose?
It depends on the device capabilities, interface requirements, team, and expected lifetime of the app. We assess those trade-offs before recommending an approach.
Can you work on an existing app?
Yes. We can review the current product and codebase, identify the constraints, and plan targeted improvements or a larger rebuild around what is worth keeping.

name: Backend & cloud
heading:
The part that
holds it all together.
copy: APIs, authentication, data, and cloud infrastructure. Built to keep your product dependable as it grows.
icon: <path d="M18 12v7M7 25v-6h22v6"/><rect x="10" y="3" width="16" height="9" rx="2"/><rect x="2" y="25" width="10" height="8" rx="2"/><rect x="24" y="25" width="10" height="8" rx="2"/><path class="accent" d="M15 7h6M28 29h2"/>
title: Backend & Cloud Development
description: Backend development, API integrations, and cloud infrastructure for growing products. Project 0 builds dependable systems and helps improve existing platforms.
intro: Your customers may never see the backend, but they feel every delay and failure. We build the APIs, data flows, and cloud infrastructure that keep a product working as its demands change.
audience: For teams building a platform, connecting services, or dealing with a backend that has become difficult to operate or change.
offers: APIs and integrations
Design and implement APIs, authentication flows, and connections between products and business systems, with clear contracts and useful error handling.
Cloud infrastructure
Set up deployment environments and automation around the product. Consider capacity, reliability, and operating costs together.
Observability and maintenance
Make it easier to understand how a system behaves. Plan logging, monitoring, and practical handover so failures can be investigated and changes made with confidence.
steps: Understand the dependencies
Map the current architecture, data, integrations, and operational requirements. Identify the constraints that will shape the implementation.
Build in manageable increments
Agree on interfaces and deliver the system in testable parts. Validate assumptions about data and traffic before they become expensive.
Make operation part of delivery
Review deployment, monitoring, documentation, and ownership alongside the code. A backend needs to be understandable after launch.
faqs: Do we need to move everything to a new platform?
Not necessarily. An architecture review can help separate genuine limitations from problems that can be solved with smaller changes.
Can you help with cloud costs?
We can review usage, architecture, and operational practices to identify opportunities. Recommendations depend on measured workloads and reliability requirements.

name: AI & machine learning
heading:
Intelligence.
With a purpose.
copy: Models, LLM integrations, and automation connected to real workflows. Useful AI, built around your product.
icon: <rect x="9" y="9" width="18" height="18" rx="3"/><path d="M13 2v7M23 2v7M13 27v7M23 27v7M2 13h7M2 23h7M27 13h7M27 23h7"/><path class="accent" d="M14 21l4-8 4 8M16 18h4"/>
title: AI & Machine Learning Development
description: AI development, LLM integrations, and workflow automation. Project 0 connects useful intelligence to real products and business processes.
intro: Start with a task worth improving. We help teams explore, evaluate, and integrate AI into products and workflows, with attention to the data, limitations, and human decisions around it.
audience: For teams exploring an AI feature, connecting a language model to an existing product, or automating a repetitive workflow.
offers: LLM integrations
Connect language models to product features and relevant context. Define the expected output, handle failures, and design a useful experience around the model.
Workflow automation
Identify repeatable steps and integrate automation with existing tools and systems. Keep review and escalation available where a person needs to make the decision.
Custom models and evaluation
Assess whether an existing model meets the task or a more tailored approach is needed. Use representative examples and explicit evaluation criteria.
steps: Define a measurable use case
Agree on the problem, available data, acceptable outcomes, and failure cases. Decide what a useful result would look like before selecting a model.
Prototype and evaluate
Test an approach against realistic examples. Compare output quality, latency, and cost, then use the results to guide the next iteration.
Integrate with the product
Connect the chosen approach to the application and its operating environment. Include monitoring, fallbacks, and user feedback.
faqs: Does every AI project need a custom model?
No. An existing model with suitable context and integration may be enough. The choice should follow the task and evaluation results.
How do you handle unreliable model output?
We define evaluation cases and failure behaviour as part of the design. Depending on the task, that can include validation, restricted actions, human review, and a fallback experience.

name: Design & UX
heading:
Feels right.
Works even better.
copy: Research, flows, interfaces, and prototypes. Shape an experience around what people actually need to do.
icon: <rect x="5" y="5" width="26" height="26" rx="1"/><path d="M5 14h26M14 14v17"/><circle class="accent" cx="5" cy="5" r="3"/><path class="accent" d="M21 21l9 3-5 2-2 5z"/>
title: UI & UX Design
description: UI and UX design for apps and digital products. Project 0 combines user research, interface design, and prototyping with practical engineering.
intro: Good design makes the next step clear. We work through how a product should behave, what people need to understand, and how the interface can support their work.
audience: For teams shaping a new product, improving a difficult user journey, or bringing consistency to an existing interface.
offers: User research and product flows
Understand the task, the people doing it, and the points where the current experience breaks down. Translate those findings into focused journeys.
Interface design
Design screens and reusable interface patterns with clear hierarchy, useful feedback, and considered responsive behaviour.
Interactive prototypes
Make important interactions tangible before development. Use prototypes to discuss behaviour, test assumptions, and resolve uncertainty.
steps: Frame the design problem
Review the existing experience and understand user goals, business needs, and technical constraints. Choose the journeys that matter most.
Explore and validate
Develop flows and prototypes, review them with the team, and use feedback to refine the direction before polishing the details.
Design for implementation
Prepare states, responsive layouts, and reusable patterns. Work with engineering to carry the intended behaviour into the finished product.
faqs: Can you design something our own developers will build?
Yes. We can work alongside an internal team and prepare designs, interaction states, and implementation guidance around its needs.
Do you redesign whole products or individual journeys?
Both. The scope can be a single difficult flow, a set of interface patterns, or a broader product redesign. We start with the problem that needs solving.

name: Digital growth
heading:
Build the product.
Grow the business.
copy: Strategy, performance marketing, SEO, and creative content that connect your work with the right audience.
title: Digital Growth & SEO
description: Digital growth strategy, SEO, performance marketing, and creative content. Project 0 helps connect your product with the people it is built for.
intro: A useful product needs to reach the right people. We connect growth strategy, search visibility, and content with the experience visitors find when they arrive.
audience: For teams preparing a launch, improving a marketing website, or making their acquisition efforts easier to measure and prioritise.
offers: Growth strategy
Clarify the audience, offer, and conversion journey. Choose channels and experiments around the business rather than treating every channel as a requirement.
Search engine optimisation
Improve technical foundations, page structure, and useful service content. Build a plan around relevant search intent and track what changes after publication.
Performance and creative content
Develop landing pages, campaign content, and creative material that communicate the offer clearly and support measurable experiments.
steps: Establish the starting point
Review the website, audience, existing activity, and available measurement. Separate missing foundations from opportunities to experiment.
Improve the journey
Work on the pages and content people use to understand the offer. Connect campaign or search intent to a relevant destination and clear next step.
Measure and refine
Review meaningful outcomes and use the results to guide the next iteration. Keep changes focused enough to learn from them.
faqs: Can you guarantee search rankings?
No. Search visibility depends on competition, content, authority, and how search engines evaluate the site. We focus on useful improvements and measurable progress.
Can growth work start before a product launches?
Yes. Positioning, landing pages, search foundations, and launch content can be prepared alongside product development.

name: Technical consulting
heading:
A clearer view.
A better next move.
copy: Architecture reviews, cost optimization, and technical strategy. Find the next step with people who build these systems.
icon: <circle cx="18" cy="18" r="14"/><path d="M18 4v4M18 28v4M4 18h4M28 18h4"/><path class="accent" d="M23 12l-3 8-8 4 4-9z"/>
title: Technical Consulting & Architecture Reviews
description: Software architecture reviews, cloud cost optimisation, and technical strategy. Project 0 helps teams make clear, practical engineering decisions.
intro: A technical decision should make the next step clearer. We review systems and plans with people who build them, then turn the findings into practical recommendations.
audience: For teams facing an architecture decision, an expensive or unreliable platform, or uncertainty about how to improve an existing system.
offers: Architecture reviews
Examine how a system is structured, where its dependencies sit, and which constraints matter. Connect findings to the product and the team operating it.
Cost and operational reviews
Review infrastructure usage and operational practices. Identify trade-offs and prioritise opportunities against reliability and delivery needs.
Technical direction
Work through options for a new product or a major change. Make the reasoning, assumptions, and consequences clear enough for the team to act on.
steps: Agree on the decision to support
Define the questions, systems, and available evidence. Establish what the review should help the team decide.
Investigate and discuss
Review architecture, code, and operational information where relevant. Discuss findings with the people closest to the system.
Deliver an actionable plan
Explain the options and trade-offs, prioritise recommendations, and identify the next steps. Continue into implementation where that is useful.
faqs: Does a review commit us to a rebuild?
No. The outcome may be a targeted improvement, a change in process, or a reason to keep the current approach. Recommendations should follow the evidence.
Can you work with our existing engineering team?
Yes. Consulting can support an internal team with an independent review, a focused investigation, or ongoing technical guidance.
